reasoning_content:
Now I've got the full picture. Plan:

1. Run the wizard non-interactively: pipe "1\n" to `bash /workspace/scripts/configure-env.sh` — profile 1 = local-dev. But note: in the local-dev profile, BUILD_OR_PULL_IMAGES=build, which builds backend and frontend images from source (takes a while, but doable). Alternatively, I can run the wizard and then set BUILD_OR_PULL_IMAGES=pull in .env to use pre-published images — but wait, start.sh: if BUILD_OR_PULL_IMAGES=pull and DEV != true, then DOCKER_BUILD_OR_PULL_DOWN="-f docker-compose.load.yml down" — but the file is docker-compose.pull.yml! Let me verify: inside start.sh:

```
if [ "$DEV" = "true" ] || [ "$BUILD_OR_PULL_IMAGES" = "build" ]; then
    build_containers+=(backend)
    DOCKER_BUILD_OR_PULL_DOWN="-f docker-compose.build.yml down"
else
    pull_containers+=(backend)
    DOCKER_BUILD_OR_PULL_DOWN="-f docker-compose.load.yml down"
fi
```

The file that exists is docker-compose.pull.yml, not docker-compose.load.yml. But this variable is only used in the DEV branch (`docker compose $DOCKER_BUILD_OR_PULL_DOWN --remove-orphans` runs only when DEV=true). When DEV != true, it just displays "Not stopping or rebuilding existing Docker containers" and doesn't use this variable.

And the actual up command is:
```
docker compose --env-file .env -f docker-compose.yml $FRONTEND_DOCKER_COMPOSE_FILE $AI_DOCKER_COMPOSE_FILE $MALWARE_DOCKER_COMPOSE_FILE -f docker-compose.build.yml up -d ...
```

Note: it always includes `-f docker-compose.build.yml`! And docker-compose.build.yml defines the backend/frontend `build:` sections. So even with BUILD_OR_PULL_IMAGES=pull, start.sh passes -f docker-compose.build.yml, and backend/frontend get `build` context defined, and `docker compose up -d backend` ends up building them (because there's no image field in build.yml, and no image field in docker-compose.yml either — so compose builds them).

So effectively, start.sh always builds backend and frontend images from source (the "pull" option in start.sh is broken / effectively always builds — docker-compose.pull.yml is not used at all in start.sh). This is a bug in the docs/script, but it means: to get the app running, we need to build both images from source. That's fine — npm ci + build for each.

Wait, actually in pull mode, is there any chance start.sh doesn't reference pull.yml? Confirmed: the main compose invocation only includes build.yml. So build is forced. The build images are:
- backend: Dockerfile.dev (npm ci --include=dev, npm run build, ts-node) — dev-mode backend runs via nodemon? Let me check entrypoint.sh.
- frontend: frontend/Dockerfile (production Next.js build with args)

Build will take a few minutes. That's acceptable.

Memory: total 7.6 GiB, 6.8 GiB available. Building Next.js + IPFS + Open WebUI… Open WebUI image is big (~10GB?). Hmm. Ollama service: not in compose. WebUI references OLLAMA_BASE_URL http://localhost:11434 — no ollama service is defined in any compose file I saw. Let me grep for an "ollama:" service across all yml files. Earlier grep only showed webui's image line and OLLAMA_BASE_URL. So no ollama service exists in compose! The guide mentions `docker compose up ipfs0 cluster0 ollama webui -d` for hot-reload development — meaning it expects an `ollama` service to exist. But it's not in docker-compose-ai.yml (only webui). This is an inconsistency, but for our purpose (basic install via start.sh) the ollama service is not needed by start.sh — start.sh only pulls `webui` (when AI is enabled), not `ollama`. So start.sh works: pulls webui image from ghcr.io.

The guide's "local-dev" profile includes AI (DISABLE_ALL_AI_FUNCTIONALITY=false) and AUTO_DOWNLOAD=true, so… the backend probably tries to download the model from the ollama service? Let me check how AUTO_DOWNLOAD works in the backend. Actually, if there's no ollama service, AI features won't fully work, but the app itself (frontend + backend + IPFS) should start. To save RAM and avoid dependency on a non-existent service, I can use the documented `--no-ai` flag to disable Ollama/Open WebUI. The guide explicitly documents `--no-ai` as an option to save RAM. But the local-dev profile default is AI enabled. Hmm, but wait: if I run ./start.sh --no-ai, the wizard runs first (with no .env yet) with default profile selection 1 (local-dev). The --no-ai flag sets DISABLE_ALL_AI_FUNCTIONALITY=true after .env is loaded (reapplied as a CLI override). So the webui service gets skipped.

Actually wait — should I keep AI enabled per local-dev profile? The task is to "install the assigned software." The core software is the document collaboration platform (frontend, backend, IPFS). AI is an optional add-on. In a 7.6GB RAM environment, the Open WebUI image is large (download ~2-3GB, runtime 1-2GB+). Risky, but disk has 952GB. RAM: frontend build (Next.js) needs ~1-2GB, backend build (npm) is fine. Running containers: ipfs (~200MB), cluster (~100MB), backend (~300MB), frontend (~150MB), webui (~1-2GB). Probably fits. But since there's no ollama service, AI analysis won't work fully anyway — the backend's AUTO_DOWNLOAD would probably try to download the model from an ollama host and fail. Since there's no ollama service in compose, I think the cleaner and documented path is to use `--no-ai` (documented flag: "disables Ollama / Open WebUI to save RAM"). This keeps the installation focused on the core software. The guide's local-dev profile includes AI, but the --no-ai flag is documented precisely for this use case. I'll go with --no-ai to save RAM.

Hmm, but let me think about whether the backend requires a webui environment variable to start. docker-compose.yml backend env: OPENWEBUI_HOST, WEBUI_SECRET_KEY, ADMIN_USER_EMAIL, ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD, AUTO_DOWNLOAD, DISABLE_ALL_AI_FUNCTIONALITY — all present in .env (generated). OK.

Build time: backend Dockerfile.dev: npm ci --include=dev (with lockfile, a few minutes), npm run build (TypeScript, ~1 min), npm install -g ts-node typescript. Frontend: npm ci (Next.js deps, ~2-4 min), build stage (next build, ~2-4 min). Total probably 10-20 min. The 600-second per-command timeout is the constraint! Each command must complete within 600 seconds. So I should run the build in the background (nohup) and poll, or use `docker compose build` with a timeout… Actually the simplest is: run start.sh in the background with nohup, redirect output to a log, and poll the log and docker ps.

Wait, but does the docker build inside start.sh have to fit in one command? No — start.sh runs as a whole process in the background; the terminal command just launches it and returns immediately. Then I poll.

Plan:
1. Generate .env: `printf '1\n' | bash scripts/configure-env.sh` — profile 1, all local-dev defaults applied (no further prompts). Check that .env gets created. Note: the wizard only asks the profile question in local-dev.

2. Run `nohup ./start.sh --no-ai > /workspace/start.log 2>&1 &` in the background… wait, --no-ai: is that "correct" per the guide? The guide says to run ./start.sh and select local-dev, and the tip says to rerun with --configure-env. The --no-ai flag is a documented option. Given that RAM is 7.6GB and there's no ollama service defined in any compose file (so the ollama part of "AI" wouldn't work anyway), I'll use --no-ai. I'll note this in the summary.

Actually, wait, let me double-check whether the ollama service is defined somewhere else, e.g. in a yml under backend or in mkdocs. Let me grep the whole repo for "ollama:". Also check the backend entrypoint and how AUTO_DOWNLOAD works.

3. Poll until containers are up: ipfs0, cluster0, truspace-backend, truspace-frontend. start.sh also waits for the IPFS API (curl localhost:5001) — with --no-ai, after `up -d` the script waits for the IPFS API, then… with LOCAL_FRONTEND=false, it just ends. Good.

4. Verify: curl http://localhost:3000 (frontend HTML), curl http://localhost:8000/api (backend health). docker ps shows everything running.

Concern: the backend `build` uses Dockerfile.dev, and entrypoint.sh runs `sh ./entrypoint.sh` — probably runs seeds and then nodemon. Let me quickly check entrypoint.sh.

Also, the backend service in docker-compose.yml has `volumes: ./volumes/clamav-scan:/scan` — start.sh creates ./volumes/clamav-scan only if MALWARE_SCANNING_ENABLED=true; otherwise mkdir list doesn't include it… actually the default dirs list is: volumes, cluster0, cluster1, db, db0, db1, general, ipfs0, ipfs1, ollama, open-webui. No clamav-scan! But the backend mounts ./volumes/clamav-scan:/scan. Docker auto-creates non-existent volume directories (as root-owned). Fine — the backend might need write access to /scan, but since we're running as root user… the backend container probably runs as root (no user specified). OK.

The LUID/LGID for the ipfs0/cluster0 user: root → 0:0. The kubo image with user 0:0 should work (data directory created as root).

Let me also check the backend entrypoint, whether the backend needs anything on startup (seeds). And check the .env that gets generated.

Another check: frontend Dockerfile build args NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL etc. — fine.

Network: Docker Hub is reachable (hello-world responded). ghcr.io — with --no-ai, we don't pull webui. Pull ipfs/kubo:v0.42.0 and ipfs/ipfs-cluster:v1.1.6, plus node:22-alpine base image.

OK, let me check the entrypoint.sh and AUTO_DOWNLOAD usage, then proceed.
